raw_response:
I've been farming these 15 mu for forty years now, so I don't sit and plan it out fancy. I keep about 3 mu in cotton — my wife and I can handle the picking if it's not more than that — and the other 12 mu runs wheat in winter, maize in summer. Same rotation my father did.

Wheat went in end of October last year. I kept some of my own seed like always, bought a little new. Before planting I put one bag of that 15-15-15 compound down for every two mu — that's what I always do. When it greens up at jointing in March I'll spread urea, about one bag per three mu. Water the wheat maybe three times if the winter is dry — once in December so it doesn't freeze out, once at jointing, once when the grain is filling. The pump electricity isn't cheap but you can't skip water on wheat.

Maize goes in right behind the wheat, middle of June, maybe the 15th or 16th if the wheat combine comes on time. No time to plow — I just run a seed drill through the stubble. Hybrid seed, has to be bought, about 25 yuan per mu. One bag of compound at planting across the field, and if it looks pale at knee-high I topdress a little urea. Water once if July is dry, skip if the rain comes. Spray once for the stem borer.

Cotton is the work crop. Planted mid-April. One bag of compound before planting, topdress urea when it flowers. Two, three sprays through summer for bollworm — can't skip those or the crop is gone. Pick through September and October, my wife and I together, maybe hire somebody for a few days if we fall behind.

No credit, no loans. Whatever cash I have from last year's cotton sale and the maize I didn't eat is what I spend. If things get tight I cut back on the topdress, not the base fertilizer.
